headline: Bass Returns, Folding Table Statue Headlines New Stadium
writeup: Buffalo Bills training camp 2026 is officially underway, with the 90-man roster taking the field Wednesday as position battles heat up across the depth chart — from the offensive line's million-dollar question up front to a two-man race at ILB and fierce competition at punter and punt returner with Tyler Bass returning from injury. The uniform excitement is running hot as leaked 'Nickel City' alternate jerseys and royal blue logo-inspired helmets have sent fans into a frenzy ahead of the official Monday reveal, while James Cook enters camp as an MVP candidate and Ed Oliver headlines a group of X-factors on defense under Jim Leonhard's watch. Pass-catching previews spotlight a crowded wide receiver and tight end room — with Dalton Kincaid sliding to TE2 in ESPN fantasy rankings and Joshua Palmer's role remaining a genuine puzzle — as the Bills' 2026 draft class looks to silence critics and promising building blocks emerge at every position. Off the field, the new $2.2 billion Highmark Stadium is drawing attention for its giant folding table statue and unique fan tributes, while new tailgate rules reshaping the parking lot experience have generated strong reactions from the Bills faithful. One Bills Live moves to a new time slot starting July 27, Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld were spotted playing pickleball before camp, Dion Dawkins gifted $10k in college scholarships, and the Bills and Sabres teamed up for a pet adoption event, rounding out a busy week in the Queen City.
